inspiration.observed_pattern: MariaDB adds an inline LIMIT clause to GROUP_CONCAT so an ordered aggregate can retain only a bounded slice of ranked values.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a segment label page. GROUP_CONCAT orders labels by score and name, then uses LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 to return the second-ranked label from each segment; the release-note wording, schema, labels, and scores are not copied.

fixture_notes: Each segment has three labels with unique score ordering. LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 must skip the top label and retain only the second-ranked label, making the aggregate slice observable rather than equivalent to an unbounded concatenation.
determinism_notes: Segment IDs, labels, scores, aggregate ordering, separator, LIMIT, and OFFSET are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE segment_label_scores (label_id INT PRIMARY KEY, segment_id INT NOT NULL, label_name VARCHAR(24) NOT NULL, label_score INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT segment_id, GROUP_CONCAT(label_name ORDER BY label_score DESC, label_name ASC SEPARATOR '|' LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1) AS second_label FROM segment_label_scores GROUP BY segment_id ORDER BY segment_id

checks.sql: SELECT label_id, segment_id, label_name, label_score FROM segment_label_scores ORDER BY label_id
